newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mixed with firmer cash hog price ideas and and an oversold condition supportive to nearbys, traders said. Pork bellies ended up in choppy trade ahead of Tuesday's reports, traders said.
Hogs closed 0.450 cent per lb higher to 0.200 lower with June up most at 81.500 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.025 to 1.125 higher with July up the least at 89.050 cents.

Hog futures held early commercial short covering gains as the market looked oversold following a recent sharp price break. The market also looked tehnically firmer after weakening recently, they said.
June posted a new low for the move early, a five-week low, then rallied to a higher end. Funds had been early sellers and continued selling through the day, which limited the recover.

Futures were trading at a sharp discount to the latest CME lean hog index at $84.45 per cwt, or the live hog equivalent of $62.49 and expectations for stronger cash hog prices Tuesday added to support. The index was well above the June lean hog futures close at 81.500 cents per lb.
Late cash hog indications from the trading floor for Tuesday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher after slipping $0.50 to $1.00 in most areas Monday, they added.
"Packers are needing a few hogs early in the week," one trader said.

Rand Financials, Rosenthal Collins and Refco bought early while Dean Witter and Prudential Securities sold. Pudential continued to sell June late against mixed support. Locals bought July late. A local actively bought June 81 puts, but option trade overall was light, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures found short covering support ahead of Tuesday's monthly USDA Cold Storage and CME Out-of-Town reports. Futures also held a major trend line on the early local carryover pressure from Friday's limit down closes and reports of continued weakness in cash bellies, traders said.

Indications on Tuesday's monthly Cold Storage report ranged from 52.2 million to 59 million lbs in U.S. warehouses on May 1 compared with 54.8 million on hand April 1 and 57.2 million in storage May 1 of last year. Net storings ranged from out 2.64 million lbs to in 4.16 million lbs, versus the 10-year average net-in product movement of 9.8 million lbs.
Rand Financials, LFG and Refco bought early with locals on both sides of the market late, traders said, and LFG sold late.
